nodes.name: DatasetService.php

nodes.languageNotes: Implements delta-compressed dataset versioning: v1 stored as a full snapshot, subsequent versions as RFC6902 JSON patches via swaggest/json-diff, with every 10th version re-materialised as a full snapshot to bound reconstruction cost.

nodes.name: DatasetService

nodes.name: update

nodes.name: updateV2

nodes.name: reconstructGwdmMetadata

nodes.name: getReconstructedMetadataEnvelope

nodes.name: computePatch
nodes.summary: Computes an RFC6902 JSON patch between two metadata payloads using swaggest/json-diff for delta-based version storage.

nodes.name: persistMetadataVersion
nodes.summary: Persists a new dataset version row, storing either a full snapshot (v1 or every 10th version) or a computed RFC6902 patch relative to the reconstructed prior version, then maps spatial coverage.

nodes.name: dispatchJobs
nodes.summary: Dispatches LinkageExtraction, TermExtraction, and search-indexing jobs after a dataset version is created or updated.

nodes.name: mapCoverage

layers.name: API / HTTP Layer
layers.description: HTTP entry points for the Gateway API: V1/V2/V3 controllers, form request validation classes, API resources, HTTP-layer traits and enums, and the MetadataManagementController facade that translates requests into GWDM metadata operations.

layers.name: Middleware Layer
layers.description: Request/response pipeline components that authenticate, authorise, and pre/post-process HTTP traffic before it reaches controllers.

layers.name: Service Layer
layers.description: Core business logic and integrations, including DatasetService and other domain services, search providers, email/mailer assembly, auditing, Mauro/TRASER metadata translation, and dataset export/import handling.

layers.name: Data / Model Layer
layers.description: Eloquent models representing the Gateway API domain (datasets, teams, applications, users, federation, etc.) together with their lifecycle observers.

layers.name: Jobs & Events Layer
layers.description: Asynchronous background processing: queued jobs (dataset link scanning, nightly tests, notifications), domain events, and their listeners.

layers.name: Console / CLI Layer
layers.description: Artisan console commands and the console kernel used for scheduled and manually-triggered maintenance tasks.

layers.name: Providers Layer
layers.description: Laravel service providers responsible for bootstrapping and wiring the application container, facades, and third-party integrations.

layers.name: Utility & Cross-Cutting Layer
layers.description: Shared, cross-cutting concerns used throughout the application: custom exceptions, contracts/interfaces, shared traits, and helper functions.

layers.name: Configuration
layers.description: Project-level Composer manifest declaring PHP/Laravel dependencies, autoloading, and build/test scripts for the Gateway API application.

tour.title: Package Manifest and Dependencies
tour.description: composer.json is the closest thing this app/-scoped codebase has to a project overview: it declares the Laravel framework version, PHP dependencies, and dev tooling (PHPUnit, PHPStan/Larastan) that shape everything else you'll see. Since the true entry point (public/index.php) lives outside this scan's scope, this manifest is our starting anchor for understanding what kind of application we're touring: a Laravel 12 API service. Keep an eye out for packages like swaggest/json-diff, which powers the dataset versioning feature covered later in the tour.

tour.title: How Requests Enter the System
tour.description: Http/Kernel.php defines the global middleware stack and named route middleware aliases that every incoming HTTP request passes through before reaching a controller. Console/Kernel.php is its sibling for the command line, registering all Artisan commands and scheduled (cron) tasks. Together these two kernels are the closest in-scope equivalent to an application entry point, since Laravel's actual bootstrap file lives outside this app/ directory.

tour.title: Wiring Routes and Services
tour.description: RouteServiceProvider.php is the central provider that loads the API route files across all three API versions (v1, v2, v3) and registers rate limiting. Laravel service providers are the framework's dependency-injection wiring layer: they run at boot time to bind services into the container before any request is handled. This is a natural next stop after the kernels, since it explains how the versioned controllers you'll meet next actually get connected to URLs.

tour.title: The Middleware Pipeline
tour.description: Building on the middleware stack registered in Http/Kernel.php, these classes show what actually happens to a request in flight: JwtMiddleware validates JSON Web Tokens or application client credentials to resolve the current user, Cors.php enforces the configured origin whitelist, and SanitizeMiddleware.php HTML-encodes incoming string input to mitigate XSS. This is the security and cross-cutting concern layer that runs before any controller logic executes.
tour.languageLesson: Laravel middleware implements a `handle($request, Closure $next)` method and can short-circuit the pipeline by returning a response instead of calling `$next($request)` — this is how auth and CORS checks reject requests before they reach a controller.

tour.title: Shared Foundations: Base Controller and Form Requests
tour.description: Http/Controllers/Controller.php (fan-in 97) is the abstract parent every HTTP controller extends, while Http/Requests/BaseFormRequest.php (fan-in 282, the single most depended-upon file in the entire app) is the base class every API request validator extends — it authorizes requests by default and formats validation failures into a consistent JSON error shape. These two files establish the shared contract that all 400+ controllers and form requests in the API layer build on, which is why they rank as the most structurally important files in the codebase.

tour.title: Core Domain Models: Dataset, User, and Team
tour.description: Models/Dataset.php, Models/User.php, and Models/Team.php are the highest fan-in domain models (72, 51, and 47 references respectively), forming the vocabulary the rest of the application speaks. Dataset.php is the central Eloquent model exposing computed attributes like linked tools, DURs, collections, and publications; User.php handles authentication and cohort-discovery permissions; Team.php represents a data custodian organisation. Nearly every controller and service you'll see from here on operates on one of these three models.

tour.title: Dataset Versioning: The Service Layer
tour.description: Services/DatasetService.php is the codebase's most architecturally significant feature: it holds all dataset business logic, including listing/searching datasets and reconstructing GWDM metadata across versions using RFC 6902 JSON patches. Models/DatasetVersion.php (fan-in 45) is the model it operates on, storing each version as either a full snapshot or a delta patch — building directly on the Dataset model from Step 6. This service-and-model pair is deliberately kept separate from the controllers so the same versioning logic can be reused across API versions.
tour.languageLesson: This is the Service Layer pattern: controllers stay thin (just HTTP concerns like validation and status codes) while DatasetService owns the actual business rules. This keeps the same logic reusable across the V2 and V3 controllers you'll see next, rather than duplicating it in each.

tour.title: Three Generations of the Same Controller
tour.description: Comparing Http/Controllers/Api/V1/DatasetController.php, V2/DatasetController.php, and V3/DatasetController.php shows the codebase's evolution in one place. V1 is a large legacy controller with CRUD, testing, export, and federation logic baked directly in; V2 delegates business logic to DatasetService.php from Step 7 for CRUD and export; V3 layers dataset version history endpoints (list versions, reconstruct a specific version) on top, exercising the RFC6902 patch reconstruction you just learned about. This progression illustrates a deliberate refactor toward thinner controllers backed by a shared service.

tour.title: Team-Scoped Datasets
tour.description: TeamDatasetController (V2 and V3) mirrors the DatasetController pattern from Step 8 but scopes every operation to a specific team, delegating to the same DatasetService.php. This is a recurring architectural pattern in the Gateway API: nearly every resource (datasets, tools, DURs, collections) has both a global controller and a team-scoped counterpart, both funneling into the same underlying service to avoid duplicated business logic.

tour.title: Metadata Translation: The MMC Facade
tour.description: MetadataManagementController/MetadataManagementController.php (MMC) is a thin facade providing static-style helpers for translating dataset metadata between schema versions via TRASER, and for validating GWDM data model types. Despite its controller-like name, it's not a real HTTP controller — it's bound into the container by MetadataManagementControllerServiceProvider.php and used internally wherever metadata needs format translation, most notably by the versioning logic in DatasetService from Step 7.

tour.title: Reacting to Change: Observers and Search Indexing
tour.description: This tightly-coupled cluster shows how the app keeps its Elasticsearch search index in sync with the database. Observers/DatasetObserver.php listens for create/update/delete/restore events on the Dataset model from Step 6 and dispatches Jobs/IndexDataset.php, a queued job that reindexes the dataset document. Both rely on Http/Traits/IndexElastic.php, a shared trait providing the actual indexing logic reused across datasets, collections, tools, DURs, and publications — this same pattern repeats for every major model in the system.
tour.languageLesson: Eloquent Observers decouple side effects (like search indexing) from model logic itself: rather than putting `$this->reindex()` inside Dataset::save(), the observer subscribes to lifecycle events, keeping the model focused on data and the observer focused on synchronization.

tour.title: Custom Exceptions and Cross-Cutting Utilities
tour.description: Exceptions/NotFoundException.php (fan-in 34) is one of several custom exception classes used throughout the controllers and services you've toured, carrying a message that gets formatted into a consistent JSON error response — the same consistency BaseFormRequest.php established for validation errors back in Step 5. This Utility layer of exceptions, contracts, and shared traits is small (15 files) but touched by nearly every other layer, making it a fitting final stop: it's the connective tissue underlying the API, middleware, service, and model layers you've now seen end to end.
